title: For a Season Called to Part
description: For a Season Called to Part in Tonic Solfa to PLEYEL'S HYMN, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 921 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Parting Hymn”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to PLEYEL'S HYMN; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: For a sea-son called to part, Let us then our-selves com-mend To the gra-cious eye and heart Of our ev-er pre-sent Friend.

lines: For a season called to part,
To the gracious eye and heart
Let thy mercy and thy care
All our souls in safety keep.
In thy strength may we be strong;
Give us, if we live, ere long,
Here to meet in peace again.

licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to PLEYEL'S HYMN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
